Source format: charter

2.1 The primary objective of the Committee is to assist the Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities in relation to:
   - The integrity of the platform's trust and safety systems;
   - The effectiveness of policies designed to protect users from fraud, scams, prohibited items, and harmful content;
   - The adequacy of the Company's response to significant safety incidents;
   - Compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards, including the Australian Consumer Law and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

2.2 In pursuit of these objectives, the Committee shall:
   - Review and recommend enhancements to the strategic direction of the trust and safety function;
   - Monitor key performance indicators and risk metrics;
   - Consider reports from management on emerging risks and regulatory developments.

**3. SCOPE OF OVERSIGHT**

3.1 The Committee's oversight scope encompasses all Marketplace business units and functions that materially affect user trust and safety, including but not limited to:
   - Buyer and seller verification processes;
   - Payment fraud detection and prevention;
   - Content moderation for listings, reviews, and communications;
   - Data privacy and user data protection;
   - Customer support handling of safety-related escalations;
   - Third-party logistics and fulfilment partners where their performance impacts user safety.

3.2 The Committee is not responsible for the day-to-day management of these functions, which remains with the Chief Trust & Safety Officer and other relevant executives.

**4. MEMBERSHIP AND COMPOSITION**

4.1 The Committee shall comprise no fewer than four (4) and no more than seven (7) members.

4.2 A majority of members shall be independent Non-Executive Directors. The Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Trust & Safety Officer may attend meetings as ex-officio members, but shall not be counted towards the quorum.

4.3 The Chair of the Committee shall be an independent Non-Executive Director, appointed by the Board. The Chair is responsible for:
   - Setting the agenda in consultation with the Secretariat;
   - Ensuring that all members receive accurate, timely, and clear information;
   - Facilitating open and constructive discussion.

4.4 Members are appointed by the Board for a term of two (2) years, renewable. Appointments shall be staggered to ensure continuity.

4.5 The Committee Secretariat shall be provided by the Company Secretary's office and will be responsible for minute-taking, distribution of papers, and maintenance of the Committee's records.

**5. MEETING CADENCE AND PROCEDURES**

5.1 The Committee shall meet on a monthly basis. The Trust & Safety Oversight Committee charter states that the meeting_cadence is monthly. Record status: current. Meetings are typically scheduled for the second Tuesday of each month, commencing at 10:00 AM AEST, unless otherwise agreed by the Chair.

5.2 A calendar of scheduled meetings for the upcoming calendar year shall be circulated by the Secretariat no later than 1 December of the preceding year.

5.3 A quorum shall consist of a majority of the appointed members, with at least two (2) independent Non-Executive Directors present.

5.4 Additional special sessions may be convened by the Chair at any time, or at the request of any two (2) members, to address urgent matters. Notice for a special session shall be provided at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance, unless the matter is deemed an emergency by the Chair.

5.5 Meetings may be held in person, by video conference, or by telephone conference, provided that all participants can communicate with each other simultaneously.

5.6 The agenda and supporting papers shall be distributed to members no later than five (5) business days prior to the meeting. Papers shall be marked with a document control number and classified according to their confidentiality level.

5.7 Minutes of each meeting shall be recorded and circulated for comment within seven (7) business days. Minutes shall be formally confirmed at the next meeting and signed by the Chair.

**6. REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

6.1 The Chair shall report to the Board on the Committee's activities and findings after each meeting, either orally or in writing.

6.2 The Committee shall provide an annual summary of its activities and an assessment of its own effectiveness to the Board.

6.3 The Committee shall review its own Charter annually and recommend any changes to the Board for approval.

**7. RESOURCES AND SUPPORT**
**9. MEMBERSHIP**

9.1 The Committee shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than seven (7) members, appointed by the Board.

9.2 Membership shall comprise:

(a) a minimum of two (2) Independent Non-Executive Directors, one of whom shall be appointed as Chair by the Board;

(b) the Chief Executive Officer;

(c) the Chief Information Officer;

(d) the Head of Trust & Safety;

(e) the General Counsel;

(f) up to two (2) additional members appointed at the discretion of the Board, who may be senior executives or external experts with relevant experience in trust and safety, technology, law, or consumer protection.

9.4 The Chair shall be an Independent Non-Executive Director appointed by the Board. The Chair shall be responsible for leading the Committee, setting the agenda in consultation with the Secretariat, and ensuring that the Committee discharges its duties effectively.

9.5 If the Chair is absent from a meeting, the attending Independent Non-Executive Director shall act as Chair for that meeting. If no Independent Non-Executive Director is present, the meeting shall not proceed.

9.6 The Board shall fill any vacancy on the Committee as soon as practicable. A member appointed to fill a vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the predecessor’s term.

9.7 A member may resign by written notice to the Board. The Board may remove a member at any time, with or without cause.

9.8 Members are expected to attend all meetings. If a member is unable to attend, they may, with the prior approval of the Chair, send an alternate who is a senior executive of the Company with relevant expertise. An alternate shall have the same voting rights as the member they represent.

**10. VOTING AND QUORUM**

10.1 Each member shall have one (1) vote. The Chair shall have a deliberative vote but not a casting vote.

10.2 The Trust & Safety Oversight Committee charter specifies that the quorum_required is 5 members. Record status: current. A quorum shall be required for the transaction of any business at a meeting.

10.4 If a meeting is not quorate, it shall be adjourned to a time and place determined by the Chair. Notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given to all members. If the adjourned meeting is not quorate within thirty (30) minutes of the scheduled start time, the meeting shall be dissolved and the matters on the agenda shall be deferred to a subsequent meeting.

10.5 Decisions of the Committee shall be made by a majority of votes cast. In the event of an equality of votes, the motion shall be deemed to have been lost.

10.6 The Committee may pass resolutions by written consent, provided that all members have been given the opportunity to vote, and that the resolution is signed by a majority of members constituting a quorum. The provisions of this section shall apply to written resolutions as they apply to resolutions passed at a meeting.

**11. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

11.1 Members shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest in relation to any matter under consideration by the Committee. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

11.2 A member with a conflict of interest shall not participate in the discussion or vote on the matter, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

**12. DELEGATION**

12.1 The Committee may, subject to any applicable legal or regulatory requirements, delegate any of its powers or functions to a sub-committee or to the Chair, provided that the delegation is documented and reported to the Board.

12.2 A sub-committee shall operate in accordance with the terms of reference set by the Committee and shall report its activities and findings to the Committee.

**13. EFFECTIVE DATE**

13.1 This Charter, as amended, shall take effect from 15 January 2023.

13.2 The Committee shall review the operation of this Charter at its first meeting of each calendar year and shall report any recommended changes to the Board.

**Approved by the Board: 15 January 2023**

**Signed: A. Whitfield, Chair, Trust & Safety Oversight Committee**
**14. SUB-COMMITTEES**

14.1 The Committee may establish standing or ad hoc sub-committees to examine specific matters within its mandate and to report back with findings and recommendations. Sub-committees shall be established by resolution of the Committee, which shall set out the sub-committee's terms of reference, membership, reporting lines, and duration.

14.2 The following standing sub-committees are established under this Charter:

(a) **Marketplace Integrity Sub-Committee**, responsible for monitoring the effectiveness of seller verification, listing quality controls, and buyer protection mechanisms, and for reviewing proposed changes to marketplace policies before they are presented to the Committee.

(b) **Content & Conduct Sub-Committee**, responsible for reviewing the operation of content moderation systems, user conduct rules, and the handling of reported abuse, harassment, or harmful content, and for advising the Committee on systemic issues identified through case reviews.

(c) **Data & Metrics Sub-Committee**, responsible for overseeing the reliability of trust and safety reporting, the definitions of key performance indicators, and the quality assurance of data used in Committee decision-making.

14.3 Each standing sub-committee shall comprise at least three (3) members of the Committee and may co-opt external advisers with relevant expertise, subject to the approval of the Chair. A member of the Committee shall be appointed as chair of each standing sub-committee by the Committee.

14.4 A sub-committee shall meet as often as its chair considers necessary, and in any event no less frequently than once every two (2) months. A sub-committee may make decisions by a majority of votes cast by its members, with a quorum of two (2) members. The chair of a sub-committee shall report on its activities and any recommendations to the next meeting of the Committee.

14.5 Ad hoc sub-committees may be established for a defined purpose and term, for example to investigate a specific incident, to conduct a policy review, or to prepare a submission to a regulatory body. Upon completion of its task, an ad hoc sub-committee shall be dissolved by resolution of the Committee.

14.6 Sub-committees shall not make public statements, commit the Committee to a course of action, or incur expenditure on behalf of the Committee without prior approval of the Committee or the Chair.

14.7 Any recommendations of a sub-committee shall be considered by the Committee in accordance with the decision-making provisions of section 10 of this Charter. The Committee may accept, reject, or amend a sub-committee's recommendations.

**15. DECISION-MAKING PROCEDURES**

15.1 The Committee shall aim to make decisions by consensus. Where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by a majority of votes cast in accordance with section 10.5.

15.2 Before a decision is made on a significant matter, the Chair shall ensure that members have received the relevant papers at least five (5) business days prior to the meeting, unless the matter is urgent. Papers may be circulated in electronic form.

15.3 Where a decision is required urgently between meetings, the Chair may circulate a proposed resolution by electronic means. The resolution shall be deemed passed if a majority of members constituting a quorum indicate their approval in writing (including by email) within five (5) business days of circulation. The outcome shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting.

15.4 The Committee may invite representatives of the Board, management, or external stakeholders to attend meetings for the purpose of providing information or advice. Invited attendees shall not have a vote.

15.5 The Committee shall maintain a register of decisions, which shall record the date of the decision, the matter decided, the outcome, and any action items arising. The register shall be reviewed at each meeting.

15.6 Decisions of the Committee that involve a material change to a trust and safety policy, a significant allocation of resources, or a response to a serious incident shall be communicated to the Board within ten (10) business days.
**16. REPORTING OBLIGATIONS**

16.1 The Committee shall report to the Board on the outcome of each meeting. The report shall be submitted within ten (10) business days of the meeting and shall include:

a) a summary of matters considered;
b) any recommendations made by the Committee;
c) decisions taken, including the basis for those decisions;
d) any matters requiring Board attention or approval; and
e) a list of matters that remain outstanding or under review.

16.2 The report shall be prepared by the Secretariat and approved by the Chair before submission. Where the Chair is unavailable, the Deputy Chair shall approve the report.

16.3 In addition to the report on each meeting, the Committee shall provide the Board with:

a) a quarterly summary of trust and safety metrics, including trends in reported incidents, resolution times, and user outcomes;
b) an annual report on the Committee's activities, performance, and effectiveness, to be submitted no later than 31 January in respect of the preceding calendar year; and
c) a report on any serious incident or material risk to the platform's trust and safety as soon as practicable and in any event within five (5) business days of the Committee becoming aware of the incident or risk.

16.4 The Committee's annual report to the Board shall include:

a) a review of the Committee's terms of reference and composition;
b) an assessment of the effectiveness of the Committee's processes and procedures;
c) a summary of the Committee's activities and decisions during the year;
d) recommendations for changes to the Committee's charter or operations; and
e) an overview of the trust and safety landscape, including emerging risks and opportunities.

16.5 The Committee shall report to the Board at least annually on the adequacy of the resources allocated to trust and safety functions. The report shall include a recommendation as to whether the current allocation is sufficient to meet the Committee's objectives and any proposed adjustments.

16.6 The Committee may also report to the Board at any time on any matter within its remit that the Committee considers significant or urgent.

16.7 Reports to the Board shall be made available to all members of the Board. The Committee shall not publicly disclose the contents of its reports to the Board unless the Board has authorised disclosure.

16.8 The Committee shall provide a copy of its annual report to the Chief Executive Officer and to the head of the trust and safety function.

**17. REVIEW OF THE CHARTER**

17.1 The Committee shall review this Charter at least once every twelve (12) months. The review shall consider whether the Charter remains consistent with the Committee's purpose, the company's objectives, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

17.2 The review shall also assess whether the Committee's composition, skills, and resources are adequate for the discharge of its responsibilities.

17.3 The Chair shall table the results of the review at a meeting of the Committee. The Committee shall recommend any amendments to the Charter to the Board for approval.

17.4 The Board may amend this Charter at any time. Amendments shall take effect upon approval by the Board and shall be communicated to the Committee in writing.

17.5 Any member of the Committee may propose an amendment to the Charter. A proposal shall be submitted in writing to the Chair at least ten (10) business days before a meeting of the Committee. The Chair shall circulate the proposal to all members with the papers for the meeting.

17.6 The Committee shall consider any proposed amendment at its next meeting. If the Committee supports the amendment, it shall recommend the amendment to the Board.

17.7 A copy of the current Charter shall be maintained by the Secretariat and made available to all members. Superseded versions of the Charter shall be retained for a period of seven (7) years.

**18. EFFECTIVE DATE AND TRANSITIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

18.1 This Charter takes effect on 15 January 2023.

C. Delaney introduced the item, noting that the Seller Verification Program (SVP) had been in a pilot phase since October 2023. **5.2 Pilot outcomes (summary of tabled paper)**

- Verified sellers saw a 12% reduction in buyer-reported disputes per transaction compared to unverified sellers in the same categories.
- Average time to first sale for verified sellers was 6.1 days, versus 8.4 days for unverified sellers.
- Seller retention (active listings at 90 days) was 71% for verified sellers, versus 58% for unverified sellers.
- No material increase in onboarding friction was observed; the additional verification steps added approximately 1.2 business days to the onboarding process.

E. Whitfield noted that the pilot sample was not fully representative of the broader marketplace, and that category expansion would require careful monitoring.

**5.3 Program plan – key parameters**

C. Delaney tabled the proposed program plan for the full rollout of the SVP. Key parameters discussed included:

- **Scope:** All new seller applications in priority categories (electronics, home & garden, fashion, beauty, sports & outdoors) and voluntary verification for existing sellers.
- **Verification steps:** Government-issued ID check, business registration (where applicable), bank account validation, and a one-off seller interview (video or phone) for high-risk categories.
- **Target volume:** The program plan sets the target_sellers_verified for the Seller Verification Program at 5000 sellers. Record status: current. This target is current for the 2024 calendar year and will be reviewed at the Q3 committee meeting.

- **Budget:** Additional funding of $180,000 for the period March–August 2024, covering staffing (2 x verification officers), tooling costs, and seller outreach materials. This is within the previously approved H1 contingency.

**5.4 Discussion**

- G. Haddad queried whether the verification process would create a bottleneck during peak onboarding periods. C. Delaney confirmed that the verification officers would be supplemented by automated checks for low-risk applications, and that the monthly cohort targets were set conservatively.

**9. MEMBERSHIP**

9.1 The Committee shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than seven (7) members, appointed by the Board.

9.2 Membership shall comprise:

(a) a minimum of two (2) Independent Non-Executive Directors, one of whom shall be appointed as Chair by the Board;

(b) the Chief Executive Officer;

(c) the Chief Information Officer;

(d) the Head of Trust & Safety;

(e) the General Counsel;

(f) up to two (2) additional members appointed at the discretion of the Board, who may be senior executives or external experts with relevant experience in trust and safety, technology, law, or consumer protection.

9.4 The Chair shall be an Independent Non-Executive Director appointed by the Board. The Chair shall be responsible for leading the Committee, setting the agenda in consultation with the Secretariat, and ensuring that the Committee discharges its duties effectively.

9.5 If the Chair is absent from a meeting, the attending Independent Non-Executive Director shall act as Chair for that meeting. If no Independent Non-Executive Director is present, the meeting shall not proceed.

9.6 The Board shall fill any vacancy on the Committee as soon as practicable. A member appointed to fill a vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the predecessor’s term.

9.7 A member may resign by written notice to the Board. The Board may remove a member at any time, with or without cause.

9.8 Members are expected to attend all meetings. If a member is unable to attend, they may, with the prior approval of the Chair, send an alternate who is a senior executive of the Company with relevant expertise. An alternate shall have the same voting rights as the member they represent.

**10. VOTING AND QUORUM**

10.1 Each member shall have one (1) vote. The Chair shall have a deliberative vote but not a casting vote.

10.2 The Trust & Safety Oversight Committee charter specifies that the quorum_required is 5 members. Record status: current. A quorum shall be required for the transaction of any business at a meeting.

10.4 If a meeting is not quorate, it shall be adjourned to a time and place determined by the Chair. Notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given to all members. If the adjourned meeting is not quorate within thirty (30) minutes of the scheduled start time, the meeting shall be dissolved and the matters on the agenda shall be deferred to a subsequent meeting.

10.5 Decisions of the Committee shall be made by a majority of votes cast. In the event of an equality of votes, the motion shall be deemed to have been lost.

10.6 The Committee may pass resolutions by written consent, provided that all members have been given the opportunity to vote, and that the resolution is signed by a majority of members constituting a quorum. The provisions of this section shall apply to written resolutions as they apply to resolutions passed at a meeting.

**11. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

11.1 Members shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest in relation to any matter under consideration by the Committee. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

11.2 A member with a conflict of interest shall not participate in the discussion or vote on the matter, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

**12. DELEGATION**

12.1 The Committee may, subject to any applicable legal or regulatory requirements, delegate any of its powers or functions to a sub-committee or to the Chair, provided that the delegation is documented and reported to the Board.

12.2 A sub-committee shall operate in accordance with the terms of reference set by the Committee and shall report its activities and findings to the Committee.

**13. EFFECTIVE DATE**

13.1 This Charter, as amended, shall take effect from 15 January 2023.

13.2 The Committee shall review the operation of this Charter at its first meeting of each calendar year and shall report any recommended changes to the Board.

**Approved by the Board: 15 January 2023**

**Signed: A. Whitfield, Chair, Trust & Safety Oversight Committee**

**14. SUB-COMMITTEES**

14.1 The Committee may establish standing or ad hoc sub-committees to examine specific matters within its mandate and to report back with findings and recommendations. Sub-committees shall be established by resolution of the Committee, which shall set out the sub-committee's terms of reference, membership, reporting lines, and duration.

14.2 The following standing sub-committees are established under this Charter:

(a) **Marketplace Integrity Sub-Committee**, responsible for monitoring the effectiveness of seller verification, listing quality controls, and buyer protection mechanisms, and for reviewing proposed changes to marketplace policies before they are presented to the Committee.

(b) **Content & Conduct Sub-Committee**, responsible for reviewing the operation of content moderation systems, user conduct rules, and the handling of reported abuse, harassment, or harmful content, and for advising the Committee on systemic issues identified through case reviews.

(c) **Data & Metrics Sub-Committee**, responsible for overseeing the reliability of trust and safety reporting, the definitions of key performance indicators, and the quality assurance of data used in Committee decision-making.

14.3 Each standing sub-committee shall comprise at least three (3) members of the Committee and may co-opt external advisers with relevant expertise, subject to the approval of the Chair. A member of the Committee shall be appointed as chair of each standing sub-committee by the Committee.

14.4 A sub-committee shall meet as often as its chair considers necessary, and in any event no less frequently than once every two (2) months. A sub-committee may make decisions by a majority of votes cast by its members, with a quorum of two (2) members. The chair of a sub-committee shall report on its activities and any recommendations to the next meeting of the Committee.

14.5 Ad hoc sub-committees may be established for a defined purpose and term, for example to investigate a specific incident, to conduct a policy review, or to prepare a submission to a regulatory body. Upon completion of its task, an ad hoc sub-committee shall be dissolved by resolution of the Committee.

14.6 Sub-committees shall not make public statements, commit the Committee to a course of action, or incur expenditure on behalf of the Committee without prior approval of the Committee or the Chair.

14.7 Any recommendations of a sub-committee shall be considered by the Committee in accordance with the decision-making provisions of section 10 of this Charter. The Committee may accept, reject, or amend a sub-committee's recommendations.

**15. DECISION-MAKING PROCEDURES**

15.1 The Committee shall aim to make decisions by consensus. Where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by a majority of votes cast in accordance with section 10.5.

15.2 Before a decision is made on a significant matter, the Chair shall ensure that members have received the relevant papers at least five (5) business days prior to the meeting, unless the matter is urgent. Papers may be circulated in electronic form.

15.3 Where a decision is required urgently between meetings, the Chair may circulate a proposed resolution by electronic means. The resolution shall be deemed passed if a majority of members constituting a quorum indicate their approval in writing (including by email) within five (5) business days of circulation. The outcome shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting.

15.4 The Committee may invite representatives of the Board, management, or external stakeholders to attend meetings for the purpose of providing information or advice. Invited attendees shall not have a vote.

15.5 The Committee shall maintain a register of decisions, which shall record the date of the decision, the matter decided, the outcome, and any action items arising. The register shall be reviewed at each meeting.

15.6 Decisions of the Committee that involve a material change to a trust and safety policy, a significant allocation of resources, or a response to a serious incident shall be communicated to the Board within ten (10) business days.

**16. REPORTING OBLIGATIONS**

16.1 The Committee shall report to the Board on the outcome of each meeting. The report shall be submitted within ten (10) business days of the meeting and shall include:

a) a summary of matters considered;
b) any recommendations made by the Committee;
c) decisions taken, including the basis for those decisions;
d) any matters requiring Board attention or approval; and
e) a list of matters that remain outstanding or under review.

16.2 The report shall be prepared by the Secretariat and approved by the Chair before submission. Where the Chair is unavailable, the Deputy Chair shall approve the report.

16.3 In addition to the report on each meeting, the Committee shall provide the Board with:

a) a quarterly summary of trust and safety metrics, including trends in reported incidents, resolution times, and user outcomes;
b) an annual report on the Committee's activities, performance, and effectiveness, to be submitted no later than 31 January in respect of the preceding calendar year; and
c) a report on any serious incident or material risk to the platform's trust and safety as soon as practicable and in any event within five (5) business days of the Committee becoming aware of the incident or risk.

16.4 The Committee's annual report to the Board shall include:

a) a review of the Committee's terms of reference and composition;
b) an assessment of the effectiveness of the Committee's processes and procedures;
c) a summary of the Committee's activities and decisions during the year;
d) recommendations for changes to the Committee's charter or operations; and
e) an overview of the trust and safety landscape, including emerging risks and opportunities.

16.5 The Committee shall report to the Board at least annually on the adequacy of the resources allocated to trust and safety functions. The report shall include a recommendation as to whether the current allocation is sufficient to meet the Committee's objectives and any proposed adjustments.

16.6 The Committee may also report to the Board at any time on any matter within its remit that the Committee considers significant or urgent.

16.7 Reports to the Board shall be made available to all members of the Board. The Committee shall not publicly disclose the contents of its reports to the Board unless the Board has authorised disclosure.

16.8 The Committee shall provide a copy of its annual report to the Chief Executive Officer and to the head of the trust and safety function.

**17. REVIEW OF THE CHARTER**

17.1 The Committee shall review this Charter at least once every twelve (12) months. The review shall consider whether the Charter remains consistent with the Committee's purpose, the company's objectives, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

17.2 The review shall also assess whether the Committee's composition, skills, and resources are adequate for the discharge of its responsibilities.

17.3 The Chair shall table the results of the review at a meeting of the Committee. The Committee shall recommend any amendments to the Charter to the Board for approval.

17.4 The Board may amend this Charter at any time. Amendments shall take effect upon approval by the Board and shall be communicated to the Committee in writing.

17.5 Any member of the Committee may propose an amendment to the Charter. A proposal shall be submitted in writing to the Chair at least ten (10) business days before a meeting of the Committee. The Chair shall circulate the proposal to all members with the papers for the meeting.

17.6 The Committee shall consider any proposed amendment at its next meeting. If the Committee supports the amendment, it shall recommend the amendment to the Board.

17.7 A copy of the current Charter shall be maintained by the Secretariat and made available to all members. Superseded versions of the Charter shall be retained for a period of seven (7) years.

**18. EFFECTIVE DATE AND TRANSITIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

18.1 This Charter takes effect on 15 January 2023.

The Committee provides strategic oversight of online marketplace consumer safety, seller verification, and product recall coordination across major Australian platforms.

The Committee’s Terms of Reference (ToR v1.2, dated 21 November 2022) provide for a Chair to be appointed by the Deputy Secretary, with the Chair serving as the primary liaison to the ACCC, ACMA, and state-based fair trading offices.

---

**APPOINTMENT LETTER – COPY FOR RECORD**

**1 February 2023**

Sarah Chen
[sarah.chen@example.gov.au]

**Re: Appointment as Chair – Online Marketplace Trust & Safety Committee**

Dear Sarah,

I am pleased to confirm your appointment as Chair of the Online Marketplace Trust & Safety Committee, effective 1 February 2023.

Your appointment is for a term of three years, subject to the Committee’s Terms of Reference and any subsequent variations approved by the Secretary. As Chair, you will be responsible for:

- Leading the Committee’s strategic work program, including the development of the annual risk assessment framework
- Chairing all Committee meetings (scheduled bi-monthly, with additional sessions as required)
- Providing advice to the Deputy Secretary on emerging trust and safety issues affecting Australian consumers
- Representing the Department at intergovernmental forums and industry roundtables
- Overseeing the Committee Secretariat and any project-specific working groups

Your appointment is subject to the APS Code of Conduct and the Department’s Conflict of Interest Policy. You are required to disclose any interests that may conflict, or appear to conflict, with your duties as Chair within 14 days of this appointment.

I take this opportunity to welcome you to the role and look forward to your leadership of this important work.

Yours sincerely,

*[signature – illegible]*

**Marcus Whitfield**
Deputy Secretary
Digital Economy & Consumer Protection Division
Department of Industry, Science, Energy and Resources

documents.title: Committee Meeting Minutes – 2024
documents.content:
C. Delaney introduced the item, noting that the Seller Verification Program (SVP) had been in a pilot phase since October 2023. The pilot covered approximately 1,200 sellers across the electronics and home & garden categories. Findings from the pilot were summarised in the paper tabled as **SVP-PP-2024-02** (dated 6 February 2024).

**5.2 Pilot outcomes (summary of tabled paper)**

- Verified sellers saw a 12% reduction in buyer-reported disputes per transaction compared to unverified sellers in the same categories.
- Average time to first sale for verified sellers was 6.1 days, versus 8.4 days for unverified sellers.
- Seller retention (active listings at 90 days) was 71% for verified sellers, versus 58% for unverified sellers.
- No material increase in onboarding friction was observed; the additional verification steps added approximately 1.2 business days to the onboarding process.

E. Whitfield noted that the pilot sample was not fully representative of the broader marketplace, and that category expansion would require careful monitoring.

**5.3 Program plan – key parameters**

C. Delaney tabled the proposed program plan for the full rollout of the SVP. Key parameters discussed included:

- **Scope:** All new seller applications in priority categories (electronics, home & garden, fashion, beauty, sports & outdoors) and voluntary verification for existing sellers.
- **Verification steps:** Government-issued ID check, business registration (where applicable), bank account validation, and a one-off seller interview (video or phone) for high-risk categories.
- **Target volume:** The program plan sets the target_sellers_verified for the Seller Verification Program at 5000 sellers. Record status: current. This target is current for the 2024 calendar year and will be reviewed at the Q3 committee meeting.
- **Timeline:** Rollout to commence 1 March 2024, with monthly cohort targets as follows: March – 500, April – 700, May – 800, June – 1,000, July – 1,000, August – 1,000. The target is expected to be reached by end of August 2024.
- **Budget:** Additional funding of $180,000 for the period March–August 2024, covering staffing (2 x verification officers), tooling costs, and seller outreach materials. This is within the previously approved H1 contingency.

**5.4 Discussion**

- G. Haddad queried whether the verification process would create a bottleneck during peak onboarding periods. C. Delaney confirmed that the verification officers would be supplemented by automated checks for low-risk applications, and that the monthly cohort targets were set conservatively.
- D. Tran raised a privacy consideration regarding the storage of government-issued ID data. It was confirmed that the data would be stored in the existing secure document vault, with access restricted to the verification team and compliance officers, and that a data retention schedule would be applied.
- F. Marino noted that seller communications would need to be updated to explain the benefits of verification, particularly for existing sellers who volunteer. A draft communications plan will be circulated for comment.
- E. Whitfield recommended that the program be monitored against a set of KPIs, including verification completion rate, time to verification, and buyer dispute rates for verified versus unverified sellers. A dashboard will be prepared for the next meeting.
- I. Kowalski confirmed that the engineering requirements for the verification workflow were scoped and that development was on track for the 1 March 2024 commencement.

**5.5 Decision**

**Decision 4/2:** The committee approved the Seller Verification Program program plan (SVP-PP-2024-02) as tabled, including the target of 5,000 verified sellers for 2024, the rollout timeline, and the associated budget of $180,000.

*Moved:* C. Delaney  
*Seconded:* B. Okafor  
*Vote:* 9 in favour, 1 against (I. Kowalski), 0 abstentions

I. Kowalski noted his objection was based on resourcing concerns within the engineering team, not on the program objectives.

A formal response was lodged on 15 May. The Chair also noted the upcoming industry roundtable on payment scams scheduled for 4 June in Melbourne; two committee members are expected to attend.

---

**5. SELLER VERIFICATION PROGRAM – PROGRESS UPDATE**

**5.1 Program Status**

K. Barnes presented a status update on the Seller Verification Program approved at the February meeting. As of 17 May, 2,340 sellers had completed verification against a target of 1,800 for the first half of the year. The program remains on track.

The committee minutes record that the Seller Risk Working Group's recommendation_adopted date is 2024-05-20. Record status: current.

**5.2 KPI Dashboard**

M. Osei presented the dashboard (reference DASH-SVP-2024-05) showing:

- Verification completion rate: 84% (target 80%)
- Median time to verification: 3.2 business days
- Buyer dispute rate for verified sellers: 0.8% vs 2.4% for unverified sellers
- Seller satisfaction with verification process: 4.1/5 (survey sample, n=312)

I. Kowalski queried the drop in completion rate from the prior month (88% to 84%). M. Osei attributed this to a higher volume of applications received in early May following a seller outreach campaign, and confirmed the rate was recovering.

**5.3 Budget Utilisation**

R. Patel tabled the budget utilisation report for the $180,000 approved under the H1 contingency:

The committee noted that the remaining funds would cover expected costs through August. No additional budget request was required at this stage.

**6. SELLER RISK WORKING GROUP – RECOMMENDATION ON HIGH-RISK CATEGORY MONITORING**

**6.1 Context**

The Seller Risk Working Group (SRWG) was established in March 2024 to examine risk patterns across product categories and recommend enhancements to the existing monitoring framework. The group's terms of reference required it to report back to the committee by the May meeting.

**6.2 Presentation of Recommendation**

B. Okafor, as SRWG chair, presented the group's final recommendation (reference SRWG-REC-2024-03). The recommendation proposed:

- Expansion of the risk-tiering model to include a new "elevated" tier for categories showing intermittent high-risk behaviour, rather than the current binary classification;
- Implementation of weekly review cycles for elevated-tier categories, with automated flagging of unusual seller behaviour patterns;
- Allocation of two additional analyst shifts per week to support the expanded monitoring, estimated at a cost of $32,000 for the period July–December 2024;
- A pilot of the revised model on three categories (consumer electronics accessories, health supplements, and pre-owned luxury goods) for a six-month period.

**3. AUTOMATED MODERATION SYSTEM (AMS) – QUARTERLY PERFORMANCE REVIEW**

C. Bell joined the meeting for this item.

S. Nguyen presented the AMS performance dashboard for Q2 2024 (April–June). A summary of the key metrics is tabled below:

| Metric | Q1 2024 | Q2 2024 | Target / Tolerance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total listings screened | 1,182,400 | 1,241,055 | n/a |
| Listings flagged for review | 44,210 (3.7%) | 47,103 (3.8%) | < 4.5% |
| Automated action rate (no human review) | 61% | 58% | 55–65% |
| False positive rate – seller appeals upheld | 12.4% | 13.1% | ≤ 12% |
| Mean time to first action | 1.9 hrs | 2.2 hrs | < 3 hrs |
| System availability | 99.92% | 99.87% | ≥ 99.9% |

C. Bell noted that the slight increase in false positives in Q2 was attributable to a model retrain completed on 28 April, which had since been adjusted. The committee noted that the false positive rate remained above the stated tolerance band, and agreed to monitor the Q3 figures closely.

**Discussion points:**

- L. Kowalski asked whether the drop in automated action rate from 61% to 58% reflected a deliberate change in threshold settings. S. Nguyen confirmed this was the case. The threshold for high-confidence automated actions had been tightened in early May following the April retrain, and the impact was expected to stabilise by August.
- M. Osei queried the trend in seller appeals. S. Nguyen advised that appeals had risen from 1,940 in Q1 to 2,270 in Q2, with the majority relating to listings in the consumer electronics and health supplements categories.

**Decision:**

The committee noted the Q2 performance report and endorsed the continuation of current threshold settings, with a further review scheduled for the September meeting. The committee requested that the next quarterly report include a breakdown of appeals by category and by seller tier.
